title: Problem Context: From C₄-Free to K_{s,t}-Free Subgraphs
content: The module header sets the stage by explaining the relationship to Erdős Problem 1008 (C₄-free subgraphs) and motivating the generalization to K_{s,t}. It provides the Kővári-Sós-Turán context (K_{s,t}-free graphs have O(n^{2-1/s}) edges), explains the probabilistic method sketch for the CFS theorem, and inventories the axioms (CFS existence and exponent optimality) vs. proved results (C₄ corollary). The docstring explicitly warns about the exponent discrepancy (1/2 from K_{2,2} vs 2/3 from parent problem), preparing the reader for the nuanced corollary section.
mathContext: Background chain: $K_{s,t}$-free $\Rightarrow$ $O(n^{2-1/s})$ edges (KST 1954) $\Rightarrow$ $K_{s,t}$-free subgraphs of size $\Omega(m^{1-1/s})$ exist (CFS 2014). For $s = t = 2$: $K_{2,2} = C_4$, giving exponent $1 - 1/2 = 1/2$ from this theorem (versus $2/3$ from the refined CFS degeneracy bound).

title: $K_{s,t}$-Freeness via Disjoint Vertex Sets
content: Defines $K_{s,t}$-freeness combinatorially: $G$ is $K_{s,t}$-free iff there do not exist disjoint vertex sets $A, B$ with $|A| = s$, $|B| = t$ and every vertex in $A$ adjacent to every vertex in $B$. This is the standard definition from extremal graph theory, equivalent to saying $G$ contains no copy of the complete bipartite graph $K_{s,t}$ as a subgraph.
mathContext: $G$ is $K_{s,t}$-free $\iff$ $\nexists A, B \subseteq V(G)$ with $A \cap B = \emptyset$, $|A| = s$, $|B| = t$, and $\forall a \in A, b \in B: ab \in E(G)$. For $s = t = 2$, this is $C_4$-freeness (in simple graphs, $K_{2,2} \cong C_4$).

title: CFS $K_{s,t}$-Free Subgraph Theorem (Axiom)
content: Axiomatizes the main result of Conlon-Fox-Sudakov (2014): for any $s \leq t$, there exists a constant $c > 0$ such that every graph $G$ contains a $K_{s,t}$-free subgraph. The proof sketch in the docstring outlines the probabilistic argument: sample vertices with probability $p = c \cdot m^{-1/s}$, bound $K_{s,t}$ copies via Kővári-Sós-Turán, delete one edge from each surviving $K_{s,t}$. The expected surviving edge count is $\Omega(m^{1-1/s})$.
mathContext: The probabilistic method: sample each $v \in V(G)$ independently with probability $p$. Expected surviving edges: $\Theta(p^2 m)$. Expected $K_{s,t}$ copies: $O(p^{s+t} n^{s+t} \cdot n^{-s})$ by KST. Setting $p \sim m^{-1/(2s)}$ balances these, yielding $\Omega(m^{1-1/s})$ surviving $K_{s,t}$-free edges.

title: Exponent Optimality via Zarankiewicz Constructions
content: States that the exponent $1 - 1/s$ is best possible, currently as a placeholder axiom (`True`). The justification is the Zarankiewicz problem: algebraic constructions (incidence graphs of projective planes over $\mathbb{F}_q$) provide $K_{s,t}$-free graphs with $\Theta(n^{2-1/s})$ edges. These extremal graphs show that no $K_{s,t}$-free subgraph of the complete graph can be much larger, establishing a matching lower bound.
mathContext: The Zarankiewicz number $z(n; s, t) = \Theta(n^{2-1/s})$ for $s \leq t$ (when $t \geq (s-1)! + 1$). This means $K_{s,t}$-free graphs on $n$ vertices have at most $O(n^{2-1/s})$ edges, and constructions achieving this bound show the exponent is tight.

title: The $C_4$ Exponent Discrepancy: $1/2$ vs $2/3$
content: The Lean docstring contains a revealing self-correction: the $K_{2,2}$ instantiation gives exponent $1 - 1/2 = 1/2$, but the parent $C_4$ result achieves $2/3$. The resolution is that the full CFS paper uses a degeneracy parameter $r$ rather than the bipartite parameter $s$. For $C_4$ (which has degeneracy 2 and $K_{2,2}$ structure), the refined formula gives $1 - 1/r = 1 - 1/3 = 2/3$, matching the known bound. This illustrates how the same forbidden subgraph can yield different extremal thresholds depending on which structural parameter (bipartite vs. degeneracy) is used.
mathContext: For $C_4 = K_{2,2}$: the crude $K_{s,t}$ bound gives $m^{1-1/s} = m^{1/2}$, while the refined CFS degeneracy bound gives $m^{1-1/r}$ with $r = 3$ for $C_4$, yielding $m^{2/3}$. The degeneracy $r$ of a graph $H$ is $\max_{H' \subseteq H} \delta(H')$ where $\delta$ is minimum degree.

title: One-Line Corollary: $C_4$ from $K_{2,2}$
content: The $C_4$ case is recovered by a single `exact` tactic instantiating the general $K_{s,t}$ theorem with $s = t = 2$. This clean specialization demonstrates the power of the generalized formulation: specific cases require no additional argument beyond parameter substitution. The `norm_num` calls discharge the side conditions $1 \leq 2$ and $2 \leq 2$.
mathContext: Since $C_4 \cong K_{2,2}$ in simple graphs, the $K_{s,t}$-free subgraph theorem with $s = t = 2$ immediately gives: every graph with $m$ edges has a $C_4$-free subgraph (though with the weaker $m^{1/2}$ bound rather than $m^{2/3}$).

title: Axiom Inventory and Formalization Roadmap
content: Summarizes the formalization: 2 axioms (CFS theorem and exponent optimality, both requiring probabilistic method), 1 proved corollary ($C_4$ from $K_{2,2}$). Notes that the key insight is the Kővári-Sós-Turán exponent's dual role: it governs both maximum edge density of $K_{s,t}$-free graphs and minimum size of $K_{s,t}$-free subgraphs. The full CFS degeneracy refinement yields better exponents for specific graphs.
mathContext: The Kővári-Sós-Turán exponent $1/s$ appears in two dual roles: the Zarankiewicz upper bound $\text{ex}(n; K_{s,t}) = O(n^{2-1/s})$ and the CFS subgraph bound $\Omega(m^{1-1/s})$. The duality arises because both are controlled by the same random sampling calculation.
